filters.name: Vertex Color Filling
filters.shortDescription: Fill vertex colors with a chosen color.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Fills the color of the vertices of the mesh with a color chosen by the user.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.help: Sets the color to apply to vertices.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: Vertex Color Thresholding
filters.shortDescription: Apply two colors according to a lightness threshold.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Colors the vertices of the mesh using two colors according to a lightness threshold (on the original color).

parameters.label: Color 1
parameters.help: Sets the color to apply below the threshold.

parameters.label: Color 2
parameters.help: Sets the color to apply above the threshold.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.help: Vertices with color above the lightness threshold become Color 2, the others Color 1.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: Vertex Color Brightness Contrast Gamma
filters.shortDescription: Adjust vertex-color brightness, contrast, and gamma.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Change the color the vertices of the mesh adjusting brightness, contrast and gamma.

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.help: Sets the amount of brightness that will be added/subtracted to the colors.

parameters.label: Contrast factor
parameters.help: Sets the amount of contrast of the mesh.

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.help: Sets the values of the exponent gamma.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: Vertex Color Invert
filters.shortDescription: Invert vertex colors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Inverts the colors of the vertices of the mesh.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: Vertex Color Levels Adjustment
filters.shortDescription: Remap an input color interval into an output interval.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: The filter allows adjustment of color levels. It is a custom way to map an interval of color into another one. The user can set the input minimum and maximum levels, gamma and the output minimum and maximum levels (many tools call them respectively input black point, white point, gray point, output black point and white point).

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.help: Gamma correction factor.

parameters.label: Min input level
parameters.help: Minimum input level.

parameters.label: Max input level
parameters.help: Maximum input level.

parameters.label: Min output level
parameters.help: Minimum output level.

parameters.label: Max output level
parameters.help: Maximum output level.

parameters.label: Red Channel
parameters.help: Apply to red channel.

parameters.label: Green Channel
parameters.help: Apply to green channel.

parameters.label: Blue Channel
parameters.help: Apply to blue channel.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: Vertex Color Colourisation
filters.shortDescription: Blend a chosen color into the existing vertex colors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Allows the application of a color to the mesh. In spite of the Fill operation, the color is blended with the mesh according to a given intensity.

parameters.label: Hue
parameters.help: Changes the hue of the mesh.

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.help: Changes the saturation of the mesh.

parameters.label: Luminance
parameters.help: Changes the luminance of the mesh.

parameters.label: Blending
parameters.help: Sets the blending factor used in adding the new color to the existing one.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: Vertex Color Desaturation
filters.shortDescription: Convert vertex colors to grayscale using a chosen method.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: The filter desaturates the colors of the mesh. This provides a simple way to convert a mesh in gray tones. The user can choose the desaturation method to apply; they are based on Lightness, Luminosity and Average.

parameters.label: Desaturation method
parameters.help: Lightness is computed as (Max(r,g,b)+Min(r,g,b))/2; Luminosity as 0.212*r + 0.715*g + 0.072*b; Average as (r+g+b)/3.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: Equalize Vertex Color
filters.shortDescription: Equalize the vertex-color histogram.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: The filter equalizes the colors histogram. It is a kind of automatic regulation of contrast; the colors histogram is expanded to fit all the range of colors.

parameters.label: Red Channel
parameters.help: Select the red channel.

parameters.label: Green Channel
parameters.help: Select the green channel.

parameters.label: Blue Channel
parameters.help: Select the blue channel. If no channel is selected the filter works on Lightness.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: Vertex Color White Balance
filters.shortDescription: Apply white balance so a chosen color becomes white.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: The filter provides a standard white balance transformation. It is done correcting the RGB channels with a factor such that, the brighter color in the mesh, that is supposed to be white, becomes really white.

parameters.label: Unbalanced white
parameters.help: The color that is supposed to be white.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: Perlin color
filters.shortDescription: Color the mesh with a Perlin-based color field.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Paints the mesh using PerlinColor function. The color assigned to vertices depends on their position in the space; it means that near vertices will be painted with similar colors.

parameters.label: Color 1
parameters.help: Sets the first color to mix with Perlin Noise function.

parameters.label: Color 2
parameters.help: Sets the second color to mix with Perlin Noise function.

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.help: Frequency of the Perlin Noise function, expressed as multiples of mesh bbox.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.help: XYZ frequency offset of the noise function.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: Color noise
filters.shortDescription: Add random noise bits independently to RGB channels.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Adds to the color the requested amount of bits of noise. Bits of noise are added independently for each RGB channel.

parameters.label: Noise bits
parameters.help: Bits of noise added to each RGB channel.

parameters.label: Only on selection
parameters.help: If checked, only affects selected vertices.

filters.name: PerMesh Color Scattering
filters.shortDescription: Assign a distinct random color to each visible mesh layer.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Assigns a random color to each visible mesh layer in the document. Colors change every time the filter is executed, but are always chosen so that they differ as much as possible.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.help: Random seed used to generate scattered colors. Zero means totally random.

filters.name: Set Mesh Color
filters.shortDescription: Set a solid per-mesh color used by the plain rendering material.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Set a solid per-mesh color that overrides the plain fill material's color for this mesh. The color is stored in the mesh data and survives undo/redo.

parameters.label: Mesh color
parameters.help: The solid color to assign to this mesh.

filters.name: Clamp Vertex Quality
filters.shortDescription: Clamp vertex quality to a chosen range or percentile crop.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Clamp vertex quality values to a given range according to specific values or to percentiles

parameters.label: Min
parameters.help: Lower clamp bound.

parameters.label: Max
parameters.help: Upper clamp bound.

parameters.label: Percentile Crop [0..100]
parameters.help: If not zero this value is used for percentile cropping of the quality values.

parameters.label: Zero Symmetric
parameters.help: If true the min/max range is enlarged to be symmetric around zero.

filters.name: Saturate Vertex Quality
filters.shortDescription: Limit the spatial gradient of vertex quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Saturate vertex quality, so that for each vertex the gradient of the quality is lower than the given threshold value (in absolute value)
The saturation is done in a conservative way (quality is always decreased and never increased)

parameters.label: Gradient Threshold
parameters.help: The maximum value admitted for the quality gradient (in absolute value).

parameters.label: Also Bake To Color
parameters.help: Also write a per-vertex color ramp after saturating quality. Disabled by default because QMeshLab automatically switches to vertex-quality visualization.

filters.name: Colorize by vertex Quality
filters.shortDescription: Map vertex quality into vertex colors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Color vertices depending on their quality field. The filter uses the same colormap sampling and range normalization used by QMeshLab quality visualization, so it can bake the current quality display into vertex colors.

parameters.label: Min
parameters.help: The value mapped to the lower end of the scale.

parameters.label: Max
parameters.help: The value mapped to the upper end of the scale.

parameters.label: Percentile Crop [0..100]
parameters.help: If not zero this value is used for percentile cropping of the quality values.

parameters.label: Zero Symmetric
parameters.help: If true the min/max range is enlarged to be symmetric around zero.

parameters.label: Color Map
parameters.help: The color map to use. Built-in QMeshLab maps match the quality visualization panel; RGB and RdPu preserve legacy VCGLib behavior.

parameters.label: Invert Color Map
parameters.help: Invert the selected QMeshLab colormap before sampling, matching the quality visualization panel. Legacy RGB/RdPu maps ignore this option.

parameters.label: Color Map Id Override
parameters.help: Optional exact QMeshLab colormap id. Leave empty for the selected Color Map enum. This is mainly used internally when baking the current view and also supports external colormaps loaded by QMeshLab.

filters.name: Quality Mapper applier
filters.shortDescription: Bake vertex quality into vertex colors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: MeshLab-compatible quality-to-color baking. QMeshLab samples the same colormap/range code used by quality visualization instead of importing the old transfer-function editor.

parameters.label: Min
parameters.help: The value mapped to the lower end of the scale.

parameters.label: Max
parameters.help: The value mapped to the upper end of the scale.

parameters.label: Percentile Crop [0..100]
parameters.help: If not zero this value is used for percentile cropping of the quality values.

parameters.label: Zero Symmetric
parameters.help: If true the min/max range is enlarged to be symmetric around zero.

parameters.label: Color Map
parameters.help: The color map to use. Built-in QMeshLab maps match the quality visualization panel; RGB and RdPu preserve legacy VCGLib behavior.

parameters.label: Invert Color Map
parameters.help: Invert the selected QMeshLab colormap before sampling, matching the quality visualization panel. Legacy RGB/RdPu maps ignore this option.

parameters.label: Color Map Id Override
parameters.help: Optional exact QMeshLab colormap id. Leave empty for the selected Color Map enum. This is mainly used internally when baking the current view and also supports external colormaps loaded by QMeshLab.

filters.name: Colorize by face Quality
filters.shortDescription: Map face quality into face colors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Color faces depending on their quality field (manually equalized).

parameters.label: Min
parameters.help: The value mapped to the lower end of the scale.

parameters.label: Max
parameters.help: The value mapped to the upper end of the scale.

parameters.label: Percentile Crop [0..100]
parameters.help: If not zero this value is used for percentile cropping of the quality values.

parameters.label: Zero Symmetric
parameters.help: If true the min/max range is enlarged to be symmetric around zero.

parameters.label: Color Map
parameters.help: The color map to use. RGB is the VCGLib default, other colormaps are sampled from Matplotlib.

filters.name: Discrete Curvatures
filters.shortDescription: Compute discrete curvature and store it in vertex quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Compute discrete curvature and store it in vertex quality. The filter does not bake colors; after it runs QMeshLab switches the view to vertex-quality color visualization.
Computed as described in:
'Discrete Differential-Geometry Operators for Triangulated 2-Manifolds'
M. Meyer, M. Desbrun, P. Schroder, A. H. Barr

parameters.label: Type
parameters.help: Choose the curvature value that you want transferred onto the scalar Quality.

filters.name: Per Face Geometric Quality
filters.shortDescription: Compute face quality from triangle shape, area, or polygonal planarity.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Computes a geometric measure for every face and stores the result in **face quality**. No colors are baked into the mesh; after completion QMeshLab switches the view to face-quality visualization.

The triangle-shape measures are scale independent and approach zero for degenerate triangles:

- **Area / squared maximum side**: `2A / Lmax²`, where `A` is triangle area and `Lmax` is its longest side. Its range is `[0, √3/2]`; an equilateral triangle reaches `√3/2`.
- **Normalized radius ratio**: `2r/R`, where `r` and `R` are the inradius and circumradius. Its range is `[0,1]`; an equilateral triangle reaches `1`.
- **Mean ratio**: `4√3 A / (a²+b²+c²)`. Its range is `[0,1]`; an equilateral triangle reaches `1`.
- **Area**: the triangle area in the mesh's squared coordinate units. This measure is not scale independent.

The planarity measures apply only to polygonal meshes represented by faux-edge triangle groups. QMeshLab fits a support plane to each polygon and assigns the same result to all its component triangles:

- **Polygonal planarity (maximum)**: maximum vertex distance from the fitted plane.
- **Polygonal planarity (relative)**: mean vertex-to-plane distance divided by the polygon's half-perimeter.

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.help: Choose the geometric measure stored in face quality.

filters.name: Per Face Texture Distortion
filters.shortDescription: Measure angular or area distortion between mesh triangles and their UV mapping.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Compares every triangle in 3D with its mapping in UV space and stores the resulting dimensionless distortion in **face quality**. No colors are baked into the mesh; after completion QMeshLab switches the view to face-quality visualization. Both per-wedge and per-vertex texture coordinates are supported, and texture image files are not required.

- **Angle distortion**: the mean relative angular error over the three corners, `mean(|θUV−θ3D| / θ3D)`. A value of `0` means that the mapping preserves all triangle angles; larger values indicate increasing conformal distortion. Uniform scaling and rigid transformations of the UV triangle do not affect this measure.
- **Area distortion**: first computes one global scale `s = ΣA3D / ΣAUV`, then evaluates each face as `|s AUV−A3D| / A3D`. A value of `0` means that the face has the globally expected texel density; larger values identify local expansion or compression relative to the mesh-wide average.

UV area is signed, matching VCGLib's distortion implementation. Folded triangles or charts with inconsistent orientation can cancel one another in the global UV-area sum; the area metric is rejected when this makes the global scale undefined. Degenerate 3D or UV triangles do not provide meaningful distortion values and should be removed before running the filter.

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.help: Choose the UV distortion measure stored in face quality.

filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Laplacian Smooth Vertex Color

parameters.help: The number of iterations of the smoothing algorithm.

filters.shortDescription: Laplacian smooth face colors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Laplacian Smooth Face Color

parameters.label: Iteration

filters.name: Transfer Color: Vertex to Face
filters.shortDescription: Transfer vertex colors to face colors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Vertex to Face color transfer

filters.name: Transfer Color: Mesh to Face
filters.shortDescription: Transfer the per-mesh color to face colors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Mesh to Face color transfer

filters.name: Transfer Color: Face to Vertex
filters.shortDescription: Transfer face colors to vertex colors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Face to Vertex color transfer

filters.name: Transfer Color: Texture to Vertex
filters.shortDescription: Sample associated textures into vertex colors.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Texture to Vertex color transfer

parameters.label: Source Texture
parameters.help: Choose which associated texture to sample. Automatic uses each face's per-wedge texture slot assignment, matching MeshLab's multi-texture behavior.

filters.name: Random Face Color
filters.shortDescription: Assign random colors to faces or faux-connected polygons.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Colorize Faces randomly. If internal edges are present they are used. Useful for quads.

filters.name: Random Component Color
filters.shortDescription: Assign a random color to each connected component.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Colorize each connected component randomly.

filters.name: Transfer Quality: Vertex to Face
filters.shortDescription: Transfer vertex quality to face quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Vertex to Face quality transfer

filters.name: Transfer Quality: Face to Vertex
filters.shortDescription: Transfer face quality to vertex quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Face to Vertex quality transfer

parameters.label: Area Weighted
